# Binary Search.

@example 33 is the sixth element, at index 5.
[-20,-8,1,6,14,33,71]
33
=> 5

@example 12 would come between 11 and 40, but it isn't in the array.
[2,5,11,40]
12
=> -1

@example 60 is the last element, at index 2.
[10,25,60]
60
=> 2

# One element: equal to target, above it, below it.
[7]
7
=> 0

[7]
3
=> -1

[7]
9
=> -1

# Two elements: target first, target last, target in the gap between them.
[-4,15]
-4
=> 0

[-4,15]
15
=> 1

[-4,15]
6
=> -1

# The extreme values allowed, at the first and the last index.
[-9999,-1,4,9999]
-9999
=> 0

[-9999,-1,4,9999]
9999
=> 3

# 0 is missing between the negative and the positive elements.
[-5,-2,3,8]
0
=> -1

# Missing, just above a middle element: a search that sets lo = mid
# instead of mid + 1 never ends.
[1,3,5,7,9,11]
6
=> -1

=> 270

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[-9999,-9997,-9996,-9993,-9991,-9989,-9987]
-9989
=> 5

@gen 2 small
[-2,1,2,6,8]
2
=> 2

@gen 3 small
[-12,-10,-9,-7,0,5,6,9]
6
=> 6

@gen 4 small
[-6,-4,4,6]
-7
=> -1

@gen 5 small
[9986,9988,9989,9993,9996,9998]
9996
=> 4

@gen 6 small
[-11,-5]
-13
=> -1

@gen 7 small
[-12,-9,-1,7,10,11]
7
=> 3
